title: Normalized ordinary and derived scalar model data
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category with a Grothendieck topology $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix a coefficient universe in which $\mathcal C$ is essentially small, sheafification of abelian presheaves exists, local bijections are precisely the sheafification equivalences, and forgetting commutative rings to rings preserves sheaves. Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings, and use their module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and standard derived localizations [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A normalized scalar model consists of the recorded derived-change-of-rings cochain model $(E,T,\epsilon)$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], an ordinary adjunction $E\dashv\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$, and a derived adjunction $T\dashv D(\operatorname{Res}_\varphi)$, subject to the following normalizations. For a module sheaf $P$, an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, $c\in S(U)$ and $x\in P(U)$, define $\operatorname{tmul}(P,U,c,x)$ as the image of $c\otimes x$ under sheafification and the specified identification of $EP$ with the ordinary sheafified tensor extension. The ordinary unit sends $x$ to $\operatorname{tmul}(P,U,1,x)$. For every pair of cochain complexes $P,K$ and every chain map $f:E(P)\to K$, the derived transpose of $\epsilon_P$ followed by $Q(f)$ is $Q$ of the degreewise ordinary transpose of $f$, followed by the inverse exact-restriction localization comparison. Here $Q$ is the localization to the derived category, and $E(P)$ means termwise application of $E$. This defines the structure and its local pure-tensor map; it does not assert existence or choose a model.
